review.rationale: Primary material independently challenged for relevance, support, actionable usefulness and limits. Changing documentation is due for re-observation after 90 days; this cadence is review policy, not a guarantee.

reasons.relevance: Versioned cases and assertions directly address repeatable prompt and model-output evaluation.
reasons.evidence: Official case and assertion documentation supports external case files and saved-output checks within their stated scope.
reasons.usefulness: A small offline pass/fail matrix with counts and separate deterministic/model assertions is actionable without candidate execution.
reasons.clarity: Deterministic checks are distinguished from model grading, factual truth and claims of broader reproducibility.

need.query: What framework tests prompts, models and application behavior against versioned cases?

claims.text: Promptfoo cases contain variables, assertions, descriptions and metadata, and may be loaded from external YAML, JSON, JSONL or CSV files, including multiple file patterns.
Promptfoo supports standalone assertions over saved outputs with --assertions and --model-outputs; deterministic assertions and model-assisted grading are distinct mechanisms.

candidates.name: Version cases and evaluate saved outputs first
candidates.reason: For a future authorized trial, commit a small case set, prompt/configuration and saved outputs. Start with deterministic assertions including known pass and fail cases; verify counts and failure reporting before any live-model evaluation.
limitations: Git versioning is a proposed reproducibility practice; model output is not guaranteed reproducible. Assertions measure only their criteria, while model grading adds an additional uncalibrated judgment dependency.
Documented capabilities acquired through primary-source research. Proposed trials have not been run; source support is separate from usefulness or comparative superiority.
